summary.prose: S004 adds revision-checked Delete for saved registrations and Discard for temporary registrations. Removal never deletes the source file, database, table or remote data, and busy or stale requests preserve the row. A committed removal stays removed when resource or credential cleanup fails; the manager receives a separate cleanup-pending state and reconciles uncertain replies with the same operation. Client layout belongs to S005, and release remains gated on the existing prerequisites and complete consumer/lease-owner integration evidence. [[c3]] [[c4]] [[c10]]

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a daemon-owned application service over the existing repository JSON registry and driver implementations. Separate saved commit, runtime activation and client refresh; use immutable credential generations and atomic JSON replacement rather than pretending the filesystem and keychain share a transaction. Temporary configurations remain in daemon memory under a workbench lease. All descriptions below are proposed architecture, not assertions of current implementation.

boundary.internal: Removal coordination for both scopes, busy/revision enforcement, confirmation state, postcommit credential cleanup retry and operation-status recovery. Never invokes source data deletion.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Safe saved-config read/patch, canonical repo validation, driver profiles, registry metadata/receipts and crash recovery, immutable secret generation staging, compatibility adapters and lease accounting foundation. Does not own temporary storage or rich manager layout. Preserve saved-only scope-local lookup and legacy pinned-family values; signed operation tickets make expiry/replay decidable after receipt pruning. Own the shared memory-only conversion/probe driver foundation, converter-cache policy/identity changes and private DuckDB lifecycle (sc8), completed before the S002/S003 branches.
Transient process probe transport, deadline/cancellation and sanitization. Uses foundational context slots without depending on s3’s session implementation.

Session open/resume/heartbeat/end, memory-only temporary overlays and receipts, trusted execution-context propagation through analyzer/tool/MCP call paths, expiry and saved/temporary collision rules. Bind the S001-owned sc8 file execution policy to session identity and expiry; S001 owns conversion, cache-policy isolation and private DuckDB lifecycle. Every native/converted kind uses that foundation rather than a branch-local converter.

Settings contributions and shared command routing, themed editor/forms, filters, dirty guards, stale-test suppression and truthful feedback in extension and external IDE. HLD has inspected the external pane, actions, service, mirrored types and Settings registrations; S005 implements the recorded plan and validates its mirrored contract before integration acceptance.

nonFunctional.performance: Draft tests have a 10-second parent-enforced deadline, with forced child reap if graceful termination fails. Workbench heartbeat is 30 seconds and expiry 90 seconds after last valid heartbeat. Mutations serialize per repo; list/filter work does not perform driver probes. LLD load tests must verify no leaked children, leases or session entries after cancellation/expiry.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns every saved/temporary config and credential decision; client labels/PIDs are not authorization. Registered-root eligibility gates management and temporary operations; saved-only analysis preserves canonical scope-local lookup without gaining mutation rights. Safe read responses return a profile allowlist and presence booleans only. Secrets, capabilities and full requests never enter logs, receipts, prompts, artifacts, telemetry or checkpoints. Temporary inputs never reach disk or keychain. A test worker receives config via private IPC and may not emit raw driver errors. Temporary file conversion, query spill and metadata/logging are part of the no-persistence boundary, including test workers.
nonFunctional.observability: Use getLogger with operation ID, safe code, repo ID, scope, revision and phase only; timing and counters for commit, activation, recovery, timeout, busy refusal and session expiry. No raw exceptions or endpoint/options. Operation status exposes committed truth even when response delivery or activation failed. Recovery-required and cleanup-pending are visible and actionable.
nonFunctional.durability: Saved JSON remains authoritative. Same-directory atomic rename/fsync commits registry, revisions and receipts together; immutable keychain generations preserve previous effective credentials until commit. Recover preparation records before enabling mutation. Issue signed 30-day operation tickets; preserve receipts through ticket expiry and pending cleanup, and distinguish expired-unreceipted from valid-not-seen after restart. Temporary state and receipts expire on explicit session end, 90-second lease loss or daemon epoch change.

api.name: RemoveConnectionRequest
api.signature: interface RemoveConnectionRequest { readonly ticket: OperationTicket; readonly operationId: string; readonly key: ConnectionKey; readonly expectedRevision: string }

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: Exact confirmed key/revision and the single signed remove operation identity.

returns.meaning: Use existing db.connections.v2.mutate with explicit mode:'remove'; committed registration:'removed' and activation:'not-applicable' mean removal, not merely a failed lookup. [[c4]]

errors.condition: Wrong scope/root/id/mode/operation, malformed or excess input, or publicPatch/credentials on remove.
Live use, revision mismatch or missing row before a new commit; replay checks the receipt first.
Existing storage, ticket, owner and compatibility failures; no legacy or saved-only fallback.

preconditions: Proposed S004 behavior; current saved/temporary mutation paths reject remove. Retain parseMutationRequest and exact ticket-target validation; the typed HLD shape gains mode:'remove' only in the existing wire adapter. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Confirmation is pure and precedes ticket issue/mutation. It identifies selected repository, ID and Saved/Temporary scope; copy says registration/owned credentials only, source data is preserved. Cancel invokes no mutation, credential or cleanup port. S005 renders this contract; S004 does not implement either client. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Saved management uses the explicit existing saved channel with registered canonical root. A presented session binding must never be stripped to choose that channel. Temporary management requires current workbench-ui owner/root/generation; unverified MCP cannot remove or inspect private state. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Feature advertisement is additive sc6 capability only after verified readiness. Old/missing capability refuses upgrade-required before issuing a removal ticket; do not interpret an unknown method as permission for legacy deletion. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

All removal/status/cleanup adapters execute on main daemon and use the existing root gate. Leases for all admitted analysis, constructor, iterator and existing-row edit-probe lifetimes must reach the same owner. Thread-local Saved pools are a known integration risk: all-consumer affinity is a release prerequisite, not established by unit tests or this design. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
postconditions: Same operation plus identical full canonical payload replays its original outcome; changed payload returns operation-mismatch. Reconcile the same ticket after transport loss before issuing another remove. Receipt lookup/MAC comparison precedes row absence/revision checks, including after same-ID recreation. [[c4]]

Under the root gate: validate live owner/eligibility/ticket, acquire the existing revision remove barrier, refuse active leases, and publish removal atomically with a fresh operation revision and receipt. A stale or busy request changes no registration, credentials, source data or receipt. [[c4]]

Logical removal and resolver invalidation occur before releasing the root gate and before awaiting cleanup. Every subsequent list/lease/acquire rejects the removed revision; do not wait for SDK close while leaving an entry resolvable. [[c4]]

Saved commit atomically removes the row and its revision from the existing JSON envelope and adds the existing-shaped removed receipt. Temporary commit synchronously removes its memory generation, decrements the shared session entry/byte budget and publishes its private removed receipt without a fabricated SafeConnection. [[c4]]

No removal path unlinks/truncates a configured source, submits DROP/DELETE, scans/deletes remote data or removes a user directory. Only existing owned metadata, obsolete application-owned credential references and exact owned runtime/conversion handles are cleanup targets. [[c4]]

Committed truth survives response loss or postcommit failure. Saved crash ambiguity is resolved through the existing preparation/receipt machinery; temporary authority and receipts disappear on session expiry/restart and cannot be reconstructed. [[c4]]

api.name: RemovalState
api.signature: interface RemovalState { readonly key: ConnectionKey; readonly operationId: string; readonly state: 'confirming'|'removing'|'busy'|'conflict'|'unknown'|'removed-cleanup-pending'|'removed'; readonly safeMessage?: string | undefined; readonly credentialCleanup?: 'complete'|'pending' | undefined; readonly resourceCleanup?: 'complete'|'pending' | undefined }

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.purpose: Strict signed remove ticket on status or cleanup retry, never a caller-supplied cleanup handle.

returns.meaning: sc6 proposed db.connections.v2.removalState({ticket}) projects committed removal and both independent cleanup phases; db.connections.v2.retryRemovalCleanup({ticket}) retries only the original operation's cleanup and returns the same projection. [[c4]]

errors.condition: Non-remove/invalid/expired-unreceipted ticket; no row-not-found shortcut to success.
Lost authority, missing feature or unavailable cleanup truth, always a fixed safe message.

preconditions: These two sc6 endpoints are proposed, bounded exact-field decoders, registered in the handler table, main-daemon method set and session allowlist together. Reuse existing canonical JSON/ticket bounds and authorize before receipt or cleanup lookup. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Saved status/cleanup use the canonical managed owner; temporary status/cleanup use only the exact authenticated session overlay and ledger. Input contains ticket only; no source path, credential ref, session handle, revision selector or arbitrary resource descriptor. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Confirming/removing/busy/conflict are pure client-facing state transitions. Server status returns unknown until a verified receipt exists; not-seen or an absent row is never treated as removed. Unknown/reconciliation-required retains same operation and retry guidance. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Do not overload sc2 credentialCleanup with runtime failures or extend the exact persisted CommittedOutcome key set. resourceCleanup is an sc6 projection of daemon-owned retirement state. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
postconditions: Removed requires both credentialCleanup and resourceCleanup complete; any pending phase maps to removed-cleanup-pending. Neither state restores a removed row or permits re-running the registration mutation. [[c4]]

Saved retries invoke existing credential journal recovery and strict runtime retirement for that receipt/revision only. Temporary retries touch memory-owned handles only; never call keychain or registry ports. [[c4]]

After a daemon restart, no SDK handle from the old process exists: runtime cleanup is complete, while saved credential cleanup is independently recovered and can remain pending. Temporary requests fail session-expired even if their ticket clock has not expired. [[c4]]

Same-ID recreation cannot redirect cleanup to the new generation; all cleanup is revision/operation/owner bound and retries are idempotent. A caller-visible timeout does not release resource ownership or imply cleanup completed. [[c4]]

api.name: SavedConnectionManagement
api.signature: interface SavedConnectionManagement { mutate(context: ManagementRequestContext, value: unknown): Promise<MutationOutcome>; status(context: ManagementRequestContext, value: unknown): Promise<OperationStatus>; removalState(context: ManagementRequestContext, ticket: OperationTicket): Promise<RemovalState>; retryRemovalCleanup(context: ManagementRequestContext, ticket: OperationTicket): Promise<RemovalState> }

returns.meaning: Add removal branches to the existing saved owner; retain create/update behavior and the sc2 receipt shape. [[c4]]

errors.condition: Existing revision/lease/storage gates and uncertain commit behavior.

preconditions: Consume the current root owner, SavedTicketAuthority, ManagedRegistry and CredentialGenerations/PreparationJournal; do not add a second transaction store, signer, lease counter or metadata schema. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Provide a narrow removal-preparation port on the existing credential owner that journals an empty ownedStagedRefs set with current registry generation before commit. cleanupRefs contains only refs owned by this application and unreferenced by every remaining row. Never read plaintext secrets to remove them. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Keep the remove barrier until durable commit classification and synchronous runtime detachment. Ambiguous commit errors preserve the journal and return reconciliation-required/recovery-required for same-ticket status, not invented success. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Existing-row edit probes must hold the same sc3 lease through child close/drain, not only config materialization. New unsaved draft probes have no selected stored revision and are not mistaken for use of an existing row. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

If registry commit throws after a possibly successful rename, do not release the remove barrier in a generic finally. Retain prepared runtime ownership and refuse resolution until same-ticket canonical receipt recovery classifies the commit; then detach or cancel the preparation as appropriate. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
postconditions: Replay returns the removed receipt before touching a recreated ID. Remove does not materialize a replacement config or allocate a credential generation. [[c4]]

Preserve unrelated registry fields, entries, pinned families, revisions and receipts. Clear any owner last-committed projection for the removed generation without altering a newly recreated one. [[c4]]

Postcommit credential deletion reuses the existing recovery loop's live-reference recheck and own-ref validation. Failed cleanup retains durable journal/receipt truth and never rolls back the row removal. [[c4]]

A removal-only strict retirement port must detach the selected pool entry and invalidate its lease revision synchronously, transfer exact SDK/build handles to a bounded cleanup-only map and retain failed closes for retry. Current closeEntry suppresses errors and must not be used as cleanup-success evidence. Saved runtime-cleanup handles contain no recoverable credential/config payload and never go to disk. [[c4]]

Keep original saved-only nested/alias read semantics and current strict legacy compatibility. v2 removal is not silently wired through legacy delete, which lacks the confirmed revision/ticket contract. [[c4]]

Proposed strict retirement bounds are 64 pending explicit-removal records per canonical root and 256 daemon-wide. Reserve capacity before commit; return busy/resource-limit rather than committing an unowned resource or evicting a pending close. Unconstructed resources need no retirement record. These limits do not block session end/shutdown from draining resources they already own. [[c4]]

api.name: SessionOperationLedger
api.signature: interface SessionOperationLedger { issue(key: ConnectionKey, mode: 'create'|'update'|'remove'): OperationTicket; status(value: unknown): OperationStatus; mutate(value: unknown, apply: (request: MutationRequest, commit: (publish: () => { readonly revision: string }) => MutationOutcome) => Promise<MutationOutcome>, assertRequest: () => void): Promise<MutationOutcome> }

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: Existing private session request; commit mode comes only from its validated ticket/request.

returns.meaning: Extend existing session issue/inspect/mutate to remove. Publication returns a revision token instead of requiring a new safe row for deletion. [[c4]]

errors.condition: Existing memory quota, owner, revision and replay rules.

preconditions: Use the same owner HMAC, in-flight map and receipts; no new global/session ledger and no temporary tombstone persistence. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
Keep existing 16384 operation-record quota and unexpired receipt retention. Remove receipts use capacity under the same bound; cleanup-pending records cannot be silently evicted. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
Temporary key/root/generation authority is revalidated after awaits and immediately before the synchronous commit callback. Owner expiry wins over ticket wall clock. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
postconditions: Derive registration:'removed', activation:'not-applicable' and credentialCleanup:'complete' from validated remove mode internally; caller JSON cannot choose outcome phases. [[c4]]
Commit callback publishes memory deletion and the receipt in one non-awaiting turn under the existing root gate; no exception after deletion can leave an unreceipted successful mutation. [[c4]]
Clear obsolete activation/cleanup bookkeeping only for the removed revision; activation retry for a removed or recreated revision cannot reopen the old driver. [[c4]]
Concurrent same-operation retries share the in-flight result; changed payload rejects. Session end revokes receipts and cancels/drains owned retirement work. [[c4]]

api.name: TemporaryConnectionOverlay
api.signature: interface TemporaryConnectionOverlay { read(id: string): SafeConnection; list(): readonly SafeConnection[]; prepareRemoval(input: { readonly id: string; readonly expectedRevision: string }, signal?: AbortSignal): object; commitRemoval(prepared: object): { readonly revision: string }; resolver(access: Readonly<ConnectionAccessContext>, authority: TemporaryUseAuthority): ConnectionResolver; close(): Promise<void> }

parameters.name: owner
parameters.purpose: Existing role/root/generation binding and full-use lifetime.

parameters.name: selected
parameters.type: { readonly id: string; readonly expectedRevision: string }
parameters.purpose: Removal candidate checked by the existing revision gate.

returns.meaning: Extend the existing overlay with a private prepare/commit-removal operation and strict revision-retirement integration; public read/list/resolver signatures stay compatible. [[c4]]

preconditions: No selected config, credentials or driver is published in sc6 state. Staging identity is opaque and owner-issued, never accepted from a wire field. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
Existing mutation barrier and CAS must prevent update/delete and lease/delete races across waits. Reject a busy selected generation before budget or receipt effects. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
Do not close the whole overlay or session to discard one row. Keep all other roots, entries, delegations, receipts and selected repository state alive. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
postconditions: Removal detaches only the selected entry, invalidates its lease state and prepared updates by revision CAS, drops its config/credential references and updates shared quotas atomically with its memory receipt. [[c4]]

Retire only the exact old revision via TemporaryDriverResources; on failure retain cleanup-only handles and safe counters, not a resolvable config. S001 sc8 file/converter close semantics are consumed unchanged. [[c4]]

Retain the removed ID's boolean reservation until its runtime cleanup completes, so same-ID creation cannot collide with failed old cleanup. Release that reservation under the same root gate after cleanup; other sessions may still retain their independent same-ID temporary rows. [[c4]]

Expiry and daemon shutdown adopt pending retirement handles into the existing session cleanup/drain path. No success or quota release may erase live owned handles; no source data or temporary state is persisted. [[c4]]

A pending explicit retirement continues to consume one of the existing 64 per-session connection/resource slots until close completes, although its live config byte budget is released on logical deletion. Share this accounting across roots, and reserve the daemon-wide removal retirement capacity before commit; session expiry transfers existing ownership without another quota admission. [[c4]]

prepareRemoval and commitRemoval are proposed internal owner ports. The object is an opaque WeakMap-backed staging token; arbitrary/copied/foreign tokens reject before effects. commitRemoval performs the synchronous deletion/lease invalidation/quota/retirement transfer, returns only a fresh operation revision, and schedules physical retirement after the ledger's synchronous receipt publication. [[c4]]

api.name: DriverPool
api.signature: interface DriverPool { prepareRemoval(id: string, oldRevision: string, operationId: string): object; commitRemoval(prepared: object): { readonly close: () => Promise<void> }; cancelRemoval(prepared: object): void }

parameters.name: prepared
parameters.purpose: Proposed opaque owner-issued token binding the selected revision, existing remove barrier and reserved retirement capacity; arbitrary/copied/foreign tokens reject.

returns.meaning: Preparation reserves cleanup ownership before commit. Verified publication synchronously detaches the old entry and returns a joined strict close; cancellation is allowed only after proving no durable removal committed. [[c4]]

errors.condition: Existing active use, entry mismatch, retirement-capacity refusal, or unresolved commit/cleanup ownership.

preconditions: These three members are proposed S004 integration ports on the existing pool, whose current source was verified in s1. No lease counter, driver cache or transaction store is duplicated. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
Caller holds existing root/remove barrier. Capacity is reserved before any registry commit; close is not started during preparation. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
Private tokens never serialize or accept user-supplied ownership. Preparing a never-constructed entry need not allocate an SDK retirement slot. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
postconditions: commitRemoval invalidates the existing lease state, detaches the exact old entry and transfers its handles synchronously before any awaited cleanup; cleanup failures keep exact handles for retry and never resurrect the row. [[c4]]
Do not use closeEntry's swallowed-error path for strict retirement. Join repeated close attempts; keep failed close ownership without dropping the driver reference. [[c4]]

On ambiguous durable commit, retain the prepared token and remove barrier until a canonical receipt/read establishes commit or noncommit. Verified commit publishes detachment; verified noncommit cancels the preparation. If classification is unavailable, new resolution remains refused and recovery-required is returned; generic finally must not reopen the old generation. [[c4]]

Bound pending explicit removal retirements at 64 per canonical root and 256 daemon-wide. Release a slot only when its exact resources close; existing expiry/shutdown ownership transfers never require a fresh quota admission. [[c4]]

dataModelChanges.details: Existing saved receipt shape remains unchanged. A remove receipt proves the exact operation's atomic row/revision removal; fresh outcome.revision is an operation tombstone identity, not a live row revision. One registry owns zero-to-many receipts; each receipt identifies exactly one key and operation. cleanupRefs are application-owned obsolete refs, never secret values. Compatibility: no extra persisted CommittedOutcome keys. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

One session owns one overlay per canonical root; each overlay owns zero-to-64 live entries across the shared session quota. A remove commit drops one live generation and writes one memory receipt. Private retired resources are no longer entries and cannot be enumerated or acquired. No cross-session state sharing or new durable schema. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

sc6-owned safe projection: key/operation/state plus optional separate credential/resource cleanup phases. A removal operation projects one current state and can own zero-to-many retired SDK/file handles. Saved credential receipts survive restart; runtime handles and all temporary states do not. Confirmation and UI transitions belong to the same model, but layout and both-client integration remain S005. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]

Daemon-only cleanup identity is exact owner/root/id/oldRevision/operation; never resolved by current ID alone. It owns zero-to-many outstanding handles with single-close/joined retry semantics. Pending closure remains reserved and bounded by existing session/resource limits; no forced eviction. Saved source creds/configs are not copied into this record. Release is blocked until all consumer paths share the required lease owner, including worker-enabled routes. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c4]]
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Proposed internal strict pool retirement port (no new persistent shape): retireRemoved(id: string, oldRevision: string, operationId: string): { readonly close: () => Promise<void> }. Detachment and ownership transfer are synchronous under the existing root/revision barrier; close joins exact cleanup ownership and retains failures. Reserve 64 records/root and 256 daemon-wide before commit.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Removal request, pure confirmation/state model, safe cleanup projection/retry and two-scope orchestration. Source-data preservation and committed-vs-cleanup truth are explicit. [[c3]] [[c4]]

Use ConnectionKey/SafeConnection, registered-root eligibility, capability negotiation and safe exact input/output validation. Append sc6 endpoints/feature support without altering old create/update or legacy behavior. [[c3]] [[c4]]

Use existing mode remove, ticket signatures/expiry, canonical request MAC, exact persisted receipt and registration removed outcome. Runtime cleanup remains separate sc6 projection; credential cleanup retains its original meaning. [[c3]] [[c4]]

Use existing root-serialized revision barriers and callback/iterator/constructor/probe leases. Main-daemon operation affinity is necessary; all-consumer cross-thread owner proof is an explicit release prerequisite, with the separate worker-crossing work left out of S004. [[c3]] [[c4]]

Use existing trusted session role/root/generation access, memory ledger quotas, expiry and cleanup owner. Discard one entry without ending the workbench or changing control/data capability lifecycle. [[c3]] [[c4]]

errorCases.detection: Existing strict mutation/ticket decoder rejects extra fields, missing expectedRevision, invalid target/mode/operation or invalid signature; compare full canonical request MAC before replay.
errorCases.response: invalid-input or operation-mismatch with fixed safe message before entry/credential/resource effects. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Row remains; correct or reopen the selected item. Never silently remint an uncertain operation.

errorCases.scenario: Active analysis, iterator, constructor or selected-row edit probe
errorCases.detection: Existing revision lease owner has active use or a mutation barrier when beginMutation(remove) runs under the root gate. All supported routes must share that owner.
errorCases.response: busy without receipt, config, credential or quota mutation. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Keep row visible; finish/cancel existing work and explicitly retry the same selected revision.

errorCases.scenario: Revision changed or selected row missing before a first commit
errorCases.detection: After checking any exact replay receipt, compare current selected entry and revision under the root gate.
errorCases.response: conflict or not-found; no source/credential cleanup. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Refresh and confirm the current row. A missing row alone is not proof this operation committed.

errorCases.scenario: Unreadable, corrupt, replaced or externally edited saved registry
errorCases.detection: Existing ManagedRegistry current snapshot and commit CAS/inode/digest/generation validation fail.
errorCases.response: registry-unreadable or recovery-required; preserve preparation and canonical operation identity when commitment is uncertain. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: No destructive fallback; reconcile status or repair management recovery before retrying.

errorCases.detection: Atomic registry publication may have occurred before fsync/readback/transport failed; caller lacks a verified removed receipt.
errorCases.response: Unknown/recovery-required projection; reuse signed ticket with status. Only an existing MAC-matched receipt establishes removed. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Keep pending operation and reconciliation guidance; do not present a fresh remove action as a retry.

errorCases.scenario: Postcommit keychain deletion failure or foreign/live credential reference
errorCases.detection: CredentialGenerations recovery checks root ownership and all live references before deletion; deleteKey or cleanup journal finalization fails.
errorCases.response: Committed removed with credentialCleanup pending; foreign/live refs are preserved and never used as destructive cleanup candidates. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Registration stays removed; retry only original owned credential cleanup through sc6.

errorCases.detection: Removal-only strict retirement awaits the exact old handle close and retains the handle when it rejects; it does not rely on the current pool helper that swallows close errors.
errorCases.response: Committed removed plus resourceCleanup pending and removed-cleanup-pending state. Failed resource remains cleanup-owned and reserved. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: No restored row or new resolution; retry cleanup without a new registration mutation.

errorCases.scenario: Temporary owner ends, expires or resumes with a newer generation
errorCases.detection: Existing role/root/generation binding and monotonic deadline guard fail before admission, after awaits or at publication; owner cancellation fires.
errorCases.response: session-expired; close admission and use existing session cleanup drains. No saved-only fallback or persisted temporary receipt. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Temporary state is unavailable after owner loss; do not claim same-ticket recovery across daemon restart.

errorCases.scenario: Ticket expired without a retained receipt or operation quota reached
errorCases.detection: Existing ticket expiry and receipt/in-flight identity checks; memory ledger or retirement capacity check before commit.
errorCases.response: reconciliation-required for expired unreceipted request, busy/resource-limit for exhausted capacity; retain pending cleanup and never evict live receipts. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Refresh/reconcile before a genuinely new action, or finish pending work before retrying.

errorCases.detection: Select retirement by original owner/root/operation/old revision and use receipt cleanup refs, never by current ID alone.
errorCases.response: Return original committed truth and clean only old unreferenced owned artifacts; reject mismatched authority. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: New registration and its credentials remain usable and unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: Unverified client, old daemon or unproven worker lease owner
errorCases.detection: Audience/capability/readiness/owner-affinity checks precede receipt/config lookup and dispatch; all-consumer integration proof is absent.
errorCases.response: unsupported-temporary, upgrade-required or closed sc6 feature gate; do not route private state through workers to obtain apparent support. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: Explicit unsupported capability rather than unsafe deletion. Separate worker-crossing work and S005 acceptance remain external prerequisites.

errorCases.scenario: Concurrent session shutdown and cleanup retry
errorCases.detection: Existing cleanup ownership and single-close/joined promise identity observe closure and cancellation after every awaited boundary.
errorCases.response: No duplicate disposal or row resurrection; retain failed handles for the existing shutdown retry path and report pending/failure honestly. [[c5]]
errorCases.userImpact: No success while an owned resource remains; shutdown backstop and source-data invariants remain unchanged.

edgeCases.input: User cancels confirmation or navigates away before confirming
edgeCases.expected: Pure state change only; no ticket issue, mutation, keychain, source file or cleanup call. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: Saved and temporary rows share an ID in historical or independent scopes
edgeCases.expected: Exact ConnectionKey and owner determine the selected row; preserve visible-namespace collision rules and unrelated owners/roots. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: Repeated identical remove before/after receipt expiry, then a new row with the same ID
edgeCases.expected: Within retained receipt validity, replay returns original removed truth without touching the new row; expired-unreceipted becomes reconciliation-required, never a best-effort second delete. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: A driver was never constructed or row has no app-owned credentials
edgeCases.expected: Remove without constructing/probing a driver or reading secret values; corresponding cleanup phases are complete. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: An imported or legacy pinned-family row contains unknown supported fields or foreign refs
edgeCases.expected: Remove selected registration only under normal revision authorization; preserve all other registry fields and foreign/live credential refs. Do not instantiate a mismatched driver just to remove it. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: Panel closure or repository switch with an in-flight cleanup
edgeCases.expected: S005 detaches view, not session ownership; original operation can still be reconciled while owner is live. No other overlay or selected repository is implicitly removed. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: Daemon restart after saved commit but before cleanup receipt finalization
edgeCases.expected: Saved journal/receipt recover credential phase. Old-process runtime handles cannot remain; do not recreate them to retry cleanup. Temporary state remains absent. [[c5]]

edgeCases.input: Concurrent remove/remove, remove/update, acquire/remove or edit-probe/remove
edgeCases.expected: Use one root and revision barrier; only valid serialized outcomes commit. Busy/stale operations have no destructive effects, and late prepared updates fail CAS after deletion. [[c5]]

invariantsToPreserve.text: Existing exact keys, MAC-bound operation replay, receipt shape and canonical root serialization remain authoritative; s1 code discovery and source-verification bundles identify these owners and their refusal branches.

Keep create/update and saved-only legacy/nested/alias behavior; only the planned remove branch is added. s1 source verification inspected current parseMutationRequest, management apply and regression fixtures.

Session capabilities, memory-only receipt/quota ownership, exact expiry and callback leases remain S003/sc3 contracts; s1 code bundle locates SessionOperationLedger, TemporaryConnectionOverlay and RevisionLeaseGate.

Logical removal cannot erase cleanup ownership; source data is outside every cleanup target. s1 source verification shows pool close suppresses errors and the existing credential journal recovery rechecks live references.
Keep S003 full-sweep failures and external/provider/client acceptance pending; s1 source-verification cites the committed full-sweep evidence and does not relabel it green.

migration.stateBefore: s1 analyzer found existing protocol, lease gate and owner classes plus explicit remove refusals. s1 source-verification inspected current saved atomic create/update publication, existing-shaped receipts and credential journal, memory-only temporary generations, and the saved close helper that suppresses close failure. sc6 removal is not currently supported or advertised; release remains disabled. [[c1]] [[c2]]
migration.stateAfter: Proposed S004 adds both owner remove branches and sc6 removal-state/cleanup retry adapters using unchanged receipt and mutation formats. Removed generations stop resolving before asynchronous cleanup. Strict retirement retains failures independently from credential cleanup. No existing source, keychain or registry migration runs automatically, and no release flag is activated by implementation. [[c7]]

migrationSteps.action: Add the sc6 types, strict decoders, pure confirmation/state model and private matching-build verifier fixtures with capability advertisement disabled. Add protocol compatibility tests before any removal is admitted. [[c7]]

Extend existing credential preparation/recovery and private runtime owner retirement ports for removal without altering persisted envelope/receipt schemas, lease counters, signing identity or session authority. Prove failure-retention and no-source-data-deletion fixtures. [[c7]]

Add saved and temporary atomic remove branches and authenticated main-daemon status/cleanup routing; retain existing create/update and strict legacy paths. All source/compiled/consumer inventories receive reviewed classifications, not an automatic hash refresh. [[c7]]

Verify real all-consumer lease affinity with worker routing enabled and full probe/iterator/constructor drains. Record any remaining worker-crossing dependency as pending and refuse unsupported routes. Do not implement the separately deferred cross-thread architecture as an S004 side effect. [[c7]]

Run each task's relevant tests, then the final fresh Node22 build and full sweep after implementation. Preserve S003's original failed sweep and isolated reruns, SQL Server/provider/foundation gaps and both-client S005 acceptance as historical/pending evidence. [[c7]] [[c11]]

Only a separately explicit release decision after all consumer, cleanup, privacy, source-preservation and external prerequisite evidence is verified may advertise saved-remove/temporary-remove and sc6 state/cleanup capabilities. This Story does not enable them. A committed user removal is not automatically reversible: recreation requires fresh user input and a new operation, never rollback of old source/config/credential material. [[c7]]

migration.backwardCompat: Keep protocol version 2 and existing signed ticket, MutationRequest, OperationStatus and persisted CommittedOutcome/CommittedReceipt shapes. Existing client methods and legacy saved read/save/delete semantics remain unchanged; no managed removal falls back to legacy delete. New clients require explicit sc6 capabilities and treat old/missing support as upgrade-required. Source and compiled evidence must describe the same build. Before downgrading, stop admission and drain current owned resources; old-process handles cannot be transferred. Saved removed receipts and empty-staging journal records retain existing-supported formats; temporary state expires on daemon restart rather than migrating. Never resurrect a removed entry or restore old credentials automatically. [[c3]] [[c7]]

alternativesConsidered.name: Extend existing mutation owners and add a narrow sc6 cleanup projection
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use existing remove tickets/mutate/status, with private retirement ownership and a separate removal-state/cleanup retry surface.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Fill the already-declared remove branch in saved and temporary owners, retaining their canonical request MAC, replay and root/lease gates. Add only sc6 removal-state and cleanup-retry projections; keep CommittedOutcome and persisted receipt shapes unchanged. Confirmation is a pure typed state projection consumed by S005. Retired SDK handles stay in daemon memory; saved obsolete credential cleanup uses the existing preparation journal, and temporary state never persists. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c3]]
pros: Smallest complete path reusing sc1/sc2/sc3/sc5 authority and recovery.
Separates committed removal from runtime cleanup without misusing credentialCleanup.
Preserves existing create/update clients and receipt formats.
cons: Needs strict removal-only retirement ports because current Saved pool close suppresses SDK close failure.
Requires explicit sc6 capability negotiation and a cleanup projection beyond generic operation status.

alternativesConsidered.name: Dedicated removal coordinator RPC with typed result envelope
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Expose one removal-specific coordinator over the existing saved and temporary owners.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an sc6 removal command/result envelope which accepts the existing signed ticket, exact key and expected revision, and delegates to the existing owner's remove branch. It owns confirmation presentation, maps replay and cleanup state, and retains the same credential journal and in-memory runtime retirement records; it does not create a new transaction store, signer or lease layer. [[c1]] [[c2]] [[c3]]
pros: One clearly scoped command can expose complete removal-specific state.
Makes future UI integration explicit without changing shared mutation outcomes.
cons: Adds a second command path alongside the existing v2 mutate removal mode.
Extra adapter and compatibility paths can drift from sc2 validation/replay behavior without changing underlying removal complexity.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: It does not close the sc3 integration gap and adds protocol adapters with partial sc1/sc2 fit compared with a1. [[c9]]

erDefinition.narrative: Removal deletes a live registration while retaining its operation receipt and, when necessary, exact cleanup-only resources. Saved receipts and credential cleanup can persist; runtime retirement and all temporary receipts stay with their existing in-memory owner. [[c4]]

ConnectionKey.description: Exact registered root, scope and ID identity used by existing protocol.

identity.description: Conceptual composite identity; never a new serialized field.

SavedRegistry.description: Existing authoritative saved registry; source data is outside this ownership graph.

receipts.description: Saved registry owns zero-to-many durable operation receipts.

SessionOverlay.description: Existing memory-only overlay owned by one live session and canonical root.

receipts.description: Overlay's owner ledger retains zero-to-many memory receipts; diagram groups the existing session ledger with its overlay.

RemovalReceipt.description: Existing-shaped operation truth for one removed generation; schema is unchanged.

key.description: Receipt points to exactly one key, even after that ID is recreated.

retired.description: Removal coordinates zero-to-many exact old runtime handles through a daemon-memory index, not persisted receipt fields.

RetiredResource.description: Cleanup-only owned SDK/file handle, never a live registration or recoverable configuration.

oldRevision.description: Exact removed generation; cleanup cannot select a new row by ID.

phase.description: Memory cleanup phase; pending remains owned until close succeeds or process exits.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Shows the required ordering between confirmation, authenticated removal, logical detachment and independent cleanup. Saved and temporary commits are alternative branches; ambiguous Saved commit retains the barrier until canonical receipt reconciliation. [[c4]] [[c5]]
